Definition: of Hebrew origin (H123); Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine:--Idumæa.
BiblicalUsage: Idumea is the Greek name for Edom, the land east and south of Palestine, and it appears once in the Gospels. In Mark 3:8 a great multitude came to Jesus from Idumea, and from beyond Jordan, drawn by what they heard he was doing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that even Edom came: the people of the old enemy's land walked to hear Jesus, and the crowd around him kept growing.
